propositions: A pure single-pass prepacked verifier produces false-positive rejections when the prepack is imperfect; a FILTER-only variant (PASS/ABSTAIN, never FAIL) eliminates false-positive rejections by construction.

A two-stage architecture combining a deterministic prepack single-pass filter with narrowed agentic fallback (via AC-block reduction at ticket load) achieves -26% token cost and -46% on real tickets versus pure-agentic verification without any false PASSes.

Filter coverage is bimodal by AC style: 90% on ACs naming greppable artifacts (tests, symbols, files) versus 0% on ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts, making coverage telemetry per AC style necessary for production adoption.

The 8000-character description admission cap in verify_completion is a deterministic failure point; any reduction mechanism must re-validate the cap after reduction and be length-neutral in adversarial edits.
False-positive rejections are impossible from filter-PASSed ACs by construction; residual production risk comes from agentic false-FAIL variance, which narrowing reduces but does not eliminate.
